slides.title: Rust close to the hardware
slides.main: Fixed types, explicit casts and bit methods make low-level code safe.

slides.title: Integer types and casts
slides.main: Sign reinterprets bits, narrowing drops the high ones, floats saturate.

slides.title: Bit methods
slides.main: Integer methods compile into one processor instruction: no need to write loops by hand.

slides.title: Byte order
slides.main: The order is in the method name: parsing binary formats becomes work with arrays.

slides.title: Size and alignment
slides.main: Rust reorders fields for size; repr(C) fixes the C order; Option<Box<T>> has no overhead.

slides.title: Floating point inside
slides.main: to_bits safely shows IEEE 754; NaN is not equal even to itself.

slides.title: Variable-length numbers
slides.main: Seven data bits per byte, the high bit means "more follows": small numbers take one byte.

slides.title: CRC32 by table
slides.main: A table of 256 values: one step per byte; the result matches zlib.crc32 in Python.

slides.title: Bit set
slides.main: Word number is i / 64, bit inside is i % 64; counting is count_ones.

slides.title: Emulator: structure
slides.main: The instruction set is an enum: match won't let you forget a new instruction.

slides.title: Emulator: execution
slides.main: Wrapping arithmetic, as in hardware; the sum 1..5 gives 15 in 19 steps, as in Python.

slides.title: Memory and traps
slides.main: Out-of-bounds access and stack overflow are values of the Trap enum, not a program crash.

slides.title: Chapter summary
slides.main: Rust expresses machine concepts with types: width, byte order, traps, all visible in code.
